money_fact: Mailchimp was built and grown as a fully bootstrapped company, with no outside investors, before Intuit acquired it for roughly $12 billion in 2021.
Upwork's Freelance Forward research has repeatedly found that independent work contributes well over $1 trillion a year to the U.S. economy.

Surveys of independent software developers from major freelance platforms consistently show experienced freelance devs in the U.S. commonly billing $75-150+/hour — well above typical salaried-equivalent pay.
money_fact_source: Common range across major freelance-rate surveys

money_fact: 37signals (makers of Basecamp) has stayed privately owned and profitable for over two decades without ever raising outside venture funding.
Y Combinator's alumni companies — including Airbnb, Stripe, and Doordash — are collectively worth several hundred billion dollars, most of which started as tiny founding teams.

The U.S. freelance workforce has grown to tens of millions of people, and research from Upwork and MBO Partners consistently finds a majority report earning as much or more than they did in traditional employment.
money_fact_source: Upwork / MBO Partners independent workforce research

money_fact: Y Combinator has funded startups with founding teams as small as one or two people that went on to become billion-dollar companies.
Multiple major freelance-platform surveys have found demand for web and software development consistently ranks among the highest-earning freelance skill categories.
money_fact_source: Common finding across major freelance-platform surveys (Upwork, Fiverr, Toptal)

money_fact: Upwork's research has found that a majority of freelancers with a college degree report earning as much as, or more than, they did in a traditional corporate job.
WhatsApp was built by a small team of fewer than 60 employees before Facebook acquired it for about $19 billion in 2014.
Basecamp built a profitable, multi-million dollar business while staying a small, self-funded team for most of its history.
PlentyOfFish was reportedly run by a single founder for years, generating tens of millions in annual profit, before selling for roughly $575 million in 2015.
Craigslist has been run by a very small team for decades while generating hundreds of millions of dollars in estimated annual revenue.
GitHub was bootstrapped by its founders for its first few years before raising outside funding, and was later acquired by Microsoft for $7.5 billion in 2018.
Shopify started as a small, self-funded project by a few founders building an online snowboard store before growing into a company worth tens of billions of dollars.
According to the U.S. Small Business Administration, the large majority of U.S. businesses are nonemployer firms — solo operations, not the exception, are the backbone of the economy.
37signals' founders have publicly stated Basecamp has been profitable every year since its founding, all without outside investors.
Industry market research consistently estimates the global freelance/gig economy at several hundred billion dollars and growing, with software and tech among its largest categories.
money_fact_source: Common estimate across gig-economy market research

money_fact: The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics has found self-employed workers in computer and IT occupations are among the higher-earning categories of self-employment in the country.
Instagram was built and grown by a team of just 13 employees before Facebook acquired it for about $1 billion in 2012.
